{
  "content": "//! Name resolution and type checking (SPEC §5.3, §5.2).\n//!\n//! Scope of the alpha (ADR 0012): primitives, `List`, `Map`, tuples, optionals,\n//! functions, closures, `data`/`enum`, `as`. Generics on user types, modules and\n//! Python interop are out.\n//!\n//! Design notes\n//! ------------\n//! * **One cause, one diagnostic.** A failed sub-expression becomes\n//!   [`Ty::Unknown`], which is compatible with everything, so `1 + f(unknown)`\n//!   reports the undefined name once instead of a type error per parent.\n//! * **No panics.** Every accessor is checked; deeply recursive input is bounded\n//!   by the parser's `E0104`, and the checker itself has no recursion guard of\n//!   its own beyond the AST's depth (ADR 0013 keeps that bounded).\n//! * Determinism: scopes are ordered vectors, so diagnostics come out in source\n//!   order.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nuse orv_syntax::{\n    Arg, BinaryOp, Block, DataDecl, EnumDecl, Expr, ExprKind, FnDecl, Item, ItemKind, Literal,\n    Pattern, PatternKind, Program, Stmt, StmtKind, UnaryOp,\n};\n\nuse crate::Diagnostic;\nuse crate::scopes::{Scopes, Symbol};\nuse crate::ty::{Ty, resolve_type};\n\n/// The result of checking a program.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct CheckResult {\n    /// Diagnostics in source order.\n    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,\n    /// The type of each top-level function, by name.\n    pub functions: HashMap<String, Ty>,\n}\n\nimpl CheckResult {\n    /// Whether any error was reported.\n    pub fn has_errors(&self) -> bool {\n        self.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.severity.is_error())\n    }\n}\n\n/// A declared user type.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum UserType {\n    /// A `data` type with named fields, in declaration order.\n    Data { fields: Vec<(String, Ty)> },\n    /// An `enum` with its variants, in declaration order.\n    Enum { variants: Vec<EnumVariant> },\n}\n\n/// One variant of an enum.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct EnumVariant {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub payload: Vec<Ty>,\n}\n\n/// Checks a whole program: names first, then types.\n///\n/// Two passes are needed because a function may call one declared later, and a\n/// `data` type may be mentioned before its declaration.\npub struct Checker {\n    diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,\n    scopes: Scopes,\n    /// Signatures of top-level functions, filled by the first pass.\n    functions: HashMap<String, Ty>,\n    /// User-declared `data`/`enum` types.\n    user_types: HashMap<String, UserType>,\n    /// Where each declared name was defined, for `E0202`.\n    declarations: Vec<(String, orv_syntax::Span)>,\n    /// The function whose body is being checked, for `return` typing.\n    current_return: Option<Ty>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Checker {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Checker {\n    /// Creates an empty checker.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            diagnostics: Vec::new(),\n            scopes: Scopes::new(),\n            functions: HashMap::new(),\n            user_types: HashMap::new(),\n            declarations: Vec::new(),\n            current_return: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Runs both passes over `program`.\n    pub fn check(mut self, program: &Program) -> CheckResult {\n        self.collect_user_types(program);\n        self.collect_signatures(program);\n        self.check_items(program);\n        CheckResult {\n            diagnostics: self.diagnostics,\n            functions: self.functions,\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Pass 1: declarations ----------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Records every `data`/`enum` and the shape of its fields.\n    fn collect_user_types(&mut self, program: &Program) {\n        for item in &program.items {\n            match &item.kind {\n                ItemKind::Data(decl) => {\n                    if !self.declare_name(&decl.name, item.span) {\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    let fields = self.data_fields(decl);\n                    self.user_types\n                        .insert(decl.name.clone(), UserType::Data { fields });\n                }\n                ItemKind::Enum(decl) => {\n                    if !self.declare_name(&decl.name, item.span) {\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    let variants = self.enum_variants(decl);\n                    self.user_types\n                        .insert(decl.name.clone(), UserType::Enum { variants });\n                }\n                ItemKind::Fn(_) | ItemKind::Use(_) => {}\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Field names and types of a `data` declaration.\n    fn data_fields(&mut self, decl: &DataDecl) -> Vec<(String, Ty)> {\n        let mut fields = Vec::new();\n        for field in &decl.fields {\n            let ty = match resolve_type(&field.ty) {\n                Ok(ty) => self.resolve_user_type(ty, field.ty.span),\n                Err(_) => {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0301\",\n                        format!(\"invalid type annotation for field `{}`\", field.name),\n                        field.ty.span,\n                    );\n                    Ty::Unknown\n                }\n            };\n            if fields.iter().any(|(name, _)| name == &field.name) {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0202\",\n                    format!(\"duplicate field `{}` in `{}`\", field.name, decl.name),\n                    field.span,\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            fields.push((field.name.clone(), ty));\n        }\n        fields\n    }\n\n    /// Variants of an `enum` declaration.\n    fn enum_variants(&mut self, decl: &EnumDecl) -> Vec<EnumVariant> {\n        let mut variants = Vec::new();\n        for variant in &decl.variants {\n            let payload: Result<Vec<Ty>, _> = variant\n                .payload\n                .iter()\n                .map(|ty| resolve_type(ty).map(|ty| self.resolve_user_type(ty, ty_span(ty, ty))))\n                .collect();\n            let payload = match variant.payload.is_empty() {\n                true => Vec::new(),\n                false => match payload {\n                    Ok(payload) => payload,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        self.error(\n                            \"E0301\",\n                            format!(\"invalid payload type for variant `{}`\", variant.name),\n                            variant.span,\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                },\n            };\n            if variants.iter().any(|v: &EnumVariant| v.name == variant.name) {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0202\",\n                    format!(\"duplicate variant `{}` in `{}`\", variant.name, decl.name),\n                    variant.span,\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            variants.push(EnumVariant {\n                name: variant.name.clone(),\n                payload,\n            });\n        }\n        variants\n    }\n\n    /// Records every function signature so calls can be checked in pass 2.\n    fn collect_signatures(&mut self, program: &Program) {\n        for item in &program.items {\n            let ItemKind::Fn(decl) = &item.kind else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if !self.declare_name(&decl.name, item.span) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let signature = self.fn_signature(decl);\n            self.functions.insert(decl.name.clone(), signature);\n            self.scopes.declare(Symbol {\n                name: decl.name.clone(),\n                ty: self\n                    .functions\n                    .get(&decl.name)\n                    .cloned()\n                    .unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown),\n                mutable: false,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The `fn(params) -> ret` type of a declaration.\n    fn fn_signature(&mut self, decl: &FnDecl) -> Ty {\n        let params: Vec<Ty> = decl\n            .params\n            .iter()\n            .map(|param| match resolve_type(&param.ty) {\n                Ok(ty) => self.resolve_user_type(ty, param.ty.span),\n                Err(_) => {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0301\",\n                        format!(\"invalid type annotation for parameter `{}`\", param.name),\n                        param.ty.span,\n                    );\n                    Ty::Unknown\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n        let ret = match &decl.ret {\n            Some(ty) => match resolve_type(ty) {\n                Ok(ty) => self.resolve_user_type(ty, ty.span),\n                Err(_) => {\n                    self.error(\"E0301\", \"invalid return type annotation\", ty.span);\n                    Ty::Unknown\n                }\n            },\n            // §5.3: a `fn` without a return annotation returns `()`.\n            None => Ty::Unit,\n        };\n        Ty::Fn {\n            params,\n            ret: Box::new(ret),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Pass 2: bodies -----------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Checks every function body.\n    fn check_items(&mut self, program: &Program) {\n        for item in &program.items {\n            match &item.kind {\n                ItemKind::Fn(decl) => self.check_fn(decl),\n                ItemKind::Data(decl) => self.check_data_defaults(decl),\n                ItemKind::Enum(_) | ItemKind::Use(_) => {}\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Checks the default values of `data` fields in the global scope.\n    fn check_data_defaults(&mut self, decl: &DataDecl) {\n        for field in &decl.fields {\n            let Some(default) = &field.default else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            let expected = self\n                .user_types\n                .get(&decl.name)\n                .and_then(|user| match user {\n                    UserType::Data { fields } => fields\n                        .iter()\n                        .find(|(name, _)| name == &field.name)\n                        .map(|(_, ty)| ty.clone()),\n                    UserType::Enum { .. } => None,\n                })\n                .unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown);\n            let found = self.check_expr(default);\n            if !self.assignable(&expected, &found) {\n                self.type_mismatch(&expected, &found, default.span);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Checks one function body in a fresh scope.\n    fn check_fn(&mut self, decl: &FnDecl) {\n        let signature = self\n            .functions\n            .get(&decl.name)\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown);\n        let ret = match &signature {\n            Ty::Fn { ret, .. } => (**ret).clone(),\n            _ => Ty::Unit,\n        };\n\n        self.scopes.push();\n        for (index, param) in decl.params.iter().enumerate() {\n            let ty = match &signature {\n                Ty::Fn { params, .. } => params.get(index).cloned().unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown),\n                _ => Ty::Unknown,\n            };\n            if !self.scopes.declare(Symbol {\n                name: param.name.clone(),\n                ty: ty.clone(),\n                mutable: false,\n            }) {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0202\",\n                    format!(\"duplicate parameter `{}`\", param.name),\n                    param.span,\n                );\n            }\n            // A default value must match the parameter's type.\n            if let Some(default) = &param.default {\n                let found = self.check_expr(default);\n                if !self.assignable(&ty, &found) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&ty, &found, default.span);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let previous_return = self.current_return.replace(ret);\n        let body = self.check_block(&decl.body);\n        self.current_return = previous_return;\n        self.scopes.pop();\n\n        // §5.3: a block's value is its last expression. The body must produce\n        // the declared return type when it ends in an expression.\n        if !ret.is_unknown()\n            && !matches!(ret, Ty::Unit)\n            && let Some(ty) = body\n            && !self.assignable(&ret, &ty)\n        {\n            let span = decl.body.span;\n            self.type_mismatch(&ret, &ty, span);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Checks a block, returning the type of its trailing expression.\n    fn check_block(&mut self, block: &Block) -> Option<Ty> {\n        self.scopes.push();\n        let mut tail = None;\n        for statement in &block.statements {\n            tail = self.check_stmt(statement);\n        }\n        self.scopes.pop();\n        tail\n    }\n\n    /// Checks a statement, returning a type only for an expression statement.\n    fn check_stmt(&mut self, statement: &Stmt) -> Option<Ty> {\n        match &statement.kind {\n            StmtKind::Let {\n                pattern,\n                mutable,\n                ty,\n                value,\n            } => {\n                let found = self.check_expr(value);\n                let expected = match ty {\n                    Some(annotation) => match resolve_type(annotation) {\n                        Ok(ty) => self.resolve_user_type(ty, annotation.span),\n                        Err(_) => {\n                            self.error(\"E0301\", \"invalid type annotation\", annotation.span);\n                            Ty::Unknown\n                        }\n                    },\n                    None => found.clone(),\n                };\n                if !self.assignable(&expected, &found) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&expected, &found, value.span);\n                }\n                self.declare_pattern(pattern, expected, *mutable);\n                None\n            }\n            StmtKind::Assign { target, value } => {\n                let found = self.check_expr(value);\n                let expected = self.check_expr(target);\n                self.check_assignable_target(target, expected.clone(), statement.span);\n                if !self.assignable(&expected, &found) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&expected, &found, value.span);\n                }\n                None\n            }\n            StmtKind::While { condition, body } => {\n                let cond = self.check_expr(condition);\n                self.require_bool(&cond, condition.span);\n                self.check_block(body);\n                None\n            }\n            StmtKind::For {\n                pattern,\n                iterable,\n                body,\n            } => {\n                let iterable_ty = self.check_expr(iterable);\n                let element = self.element_type(&iterable_ty, iterable.span);\n                self.scopes.push();\n                self.declare_pattern(pattern, element, false);\n                let mut tail = None;\n                for statement in &body.statements {\n                    tail = self.check_stmt(statement);\n                }\n                self.scopes.pop();\n                tail\n            }\n            StmtKind::Return(value) => {\n                let found = match value {\n                    Some(value) => self.check_expr(value),\n                    None => Ty::Unit,\n                };\n                let expected = self.current_return.clone().unwrap_or(Ty::Unit);\n                if !expected.is_unknown() && !self.assignable(&expected, &found) {\n                    let span = value.as_ref().map(|e| e.span).unwrap_or(statement.span);\n                    self.type_mismatch(&expected, &found, span);\n                }\n                None\n            }\n            StmtKind::Break | StmtKind::Continue => None,\n            StmtKind::Fail(value) => {\n                self.check_expr(value);\n                None\n            }\n            StmtKind::Expr(expr) => Some(self.check_expr(expr)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Declares the names bound by `pattern` with the given type.\n    fn declare_pattern(&mut self, pattern: &Pattern, ty: Ty, mutable: bool) {\n        match &pattern.kind {\n            PatternKind::Wildcard => {}\n            PatternKind::Bind(name) => {\n                if !self.scopes.declare(Symbol {\n                    name: name.clone(),\n                    ty,\n                    mutable,\n                }) {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0202\",\n                        format!(\"duplicate definition of `{name}`\"),\n                        pattern.span,\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n            PatternKind::Literal(_) | PatternKind::Variant { .. } => {\n                // Only `let PATTERN =` uses this path, and `let` takes a bound\n                // name (§5.2 `let_stmt`), so these cannot appear here.\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Checks that an assignment target is a mutable binding or a place.\n    fn check_assignable_target(\n        &mut self,\n        target: &Expr,\n        _ty: Ty,\n        statement_span: orv_syntax::Span,\n    ) {\n        match &target.kind {\n            ExprKind::Ident(name) => match self.scopes.lookup(name) {\n                Some(symbol) if !symbol.mutable => {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0230\",\n                        format!(\"cannot assign to immutable `{name}`\"),\n                        statement_span,\n                    );\n                }\n                Some(_) => {}\n                None => {\n                    // The undefined name is already reported by `check_expr`.\n                }\n            },\n            // `u.field = v` and `xs[i] = v` are allowed: the place is mutable\n            // even when the binding is not (§5.2 `lvalue`).\n            ExprKind::Field { .. } | ExprKind::Index { .. } | ExprKind::OptionalField { .. } => {}\n            _ => {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0230\",\n                    \"invalid assignment target\",\n                    statement_span,\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The element type iterated by `for`.\n    fn element_type(&mut self, ty: &Ty, span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        match ty {\n            Ty::List(element) => (**element).clone(),\n            Ty::Map(key, _) => (**key).clone(),\n            Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n            other => {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0301\",\n                    format!(\"`{other}` is not iterable\"),\n                    span,\n                );\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Expressions --------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Infers the type of an expression, reporting what it can.\n    pub fn check_expr(&mut self, expr: &Expr) -> Ty {\n        match &expr.kind {\n            ExprKind::Literal(literal) => self.literal_type(literal, expr.span),\n            ExprKind::Ident(name) => self.ident_type(name, expr.span),\n            ExprKind::Paren(inner) => self.check_expr(inner),\n            ExprKind::Block(block) => self.check_block(block).unwrap_or(Ty::Unit),\n            ExprKind::Field { receiver, name } => {\n                let receiver_ty = self.check_expr(receiver);\n                self.field_type(&receiver_ty, name, expr.span)\n            }\n            ExprKind::OptionalField { receiver, name } => {\n                let receiver_ty = self.check_expr(receiver);\n                let inner = match &receiver_ty {\n                    Ty::Optional(inner) => (**inner).clone(),\n                    other => other.clone(),\n                };\n                let field = self.field_type(&inner, name, expr.span);\n                Ty::Optional(Box::new(field))\n            }\n            ExprKind::Call { callee, args } => self.check_call(callee, args, expr.span),\n            ExprKind::Index { receiver, index } => {\n                let receiver_ty = self.check_expr(receiver);\n                let index_ty = self.check_expr(index);\n                self.index_type(&receiver_ty, &index_ty, expr.span)\n            }\n            ExprKind::Unary { op, operand } => {\n                let operand_ty = self.check_expr(operand);\n                self.unary_type(*op, &operand_ty, expr.span)\n            }\n            ExprKind::Binary { op, left, right } => {\n                let left_ty = self.check_expr(left);\n                let right_ty = self.check_expr(right);\n                self.binary_type(*op, &left_ty, &right_ty, expr.span)\n            }\n            ExprKind::Cast { expr: inner, ty } => {\n                self.check_expr(inner);\n                match resolve_type(ty) {\n                    Ok(ty) => self.resolve_user_type(ty, ty_span_of(ty.clone(), ty_span(ty.clone(), ty.span))),\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        self.error(\"E0311\", \"invalid cast target type\", ty.span);\n                        Ty::Unknown\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            ExprKind::Tuple(elements) => {\n                Ty::Tuple(elements.iter().map(|e| self.check_expr(e)).collect())\n            }\n            ExprKind::List(elements) => {\n                let mut element_ty: Option<Ty> = None;\n                for element in elements {\n                    let found = self.check_expr(element);\n                    element_ty = Some(match element_ty {\n                        None => found,\n                        Some(previous) => self.unify(&previous, &found, element.span),\n                    });\n                }\n                Ty::List(Box::new(element_ty.unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown)))\n            }\n            ExprKind::Map(entries) => {\n                let mut key_ty: Option<Ty> = None;\n                let mut value_ty: Option<Ty> = None;\n                for (key, value) in entries {\n                    let found_key = self.check_expr(key);\n                    let found_value = self.check_expr(value);\n                    key_ty = Some(match key_ty {\n                        None => found_key,\n                        Some(previous) => self.unify(&previous, &found_key, key.span),\n                    });\n                    value_ty = Some(match value_ty {\n                        None => found_value,\n                        Some(previous) => self.unify(&previous, &found_value, value.span),\n                    });\n                }\n                Ty::Map(\n                    Box::new(key_ty.unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown)),\n                    Box::new(value_ty.unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown)),\n                )\n            }\n            ExprKind::If {\n                condition,\n                then_block,\n                else_branch,\n            } => {\n                let cond = self.check_expr(condition);\n                self.require_bool(&cond, condition.span);\n                let then_ty = self.check_block(then_block).unwrap_or(Ty::Unit);\n                match else_branch {\n                    Some(branch) => {\n                        let else_ty = self.check_expr(branch);\n                        self.unify(&then_ty, &else_ty, branch.span)\n                    }\n                    // Without `else`, an `if` used as a value is `()`.\n                    None => Ty::Unit,\n                }\n            }\n            ExprKind::Match { scrutinee, arms } => {\n                let scrutinee_ty = self.check_expr(scrutinee);\n                let mut result: Option<Ty> = None;\n                for arm in arms {\n                    self.check_pattern(&arm.pattern, &scrutinee_ty);\n                    if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {\n                        let guard_ty = self.check_expr(guard);\n                        self.require_bool(&guard_ty, guard.span);\n                    }\n                    let arm_ty = self.check_expr(&arm.body);\n                    result = Some(match result {\n                        None => arm_ty,\n                        Some(previous) => self.unify(&previous, &arm_ty, arm.body.span),\n                    });\n                }\n                result.unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown)\n            }\n            ExprKind::Try(inner) => {\n                let inner_ty = self.check_expr(inner);\n                Ty::Result(Box::new(inner_ty))\n            }\n            ExprKind::Fail(_) => {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0407\",\n                    \"`fail` is not supported in 0.1.0-alpha\",\n                    expr.span,\n                );\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n            ExprKind::Lambda { params, body } => {\n                // §5.3: a lambda infers its parameter types from the expected\n                // type; without that context it is `E0310`.\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0310\",\n                    \"cannot infer the type of this lambda without an expected type\",\n                    expr.span,\n                );\n                let _ = (params, body);\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of a literal.\n    fn literal_type(&mut self, literal: &Literal, _span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        match literal {\n            Literal::Int(_) => Ty::Int,\n            Literal::Float(_) => Ty::Float,\n            Literal::Bool(_) => Ty::Bool,\n            Literal::None => Ty::Optional(Box::new(Ty::Unknown)),\n            // Interpolation parts are not sub-parsed in the alpha (ADR 0008\n            // rule 4 / ADR 0012), so a string is always `Str`.\n            Literal::Str(_) => Ty::Str,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of a name.\n    fn ident_type(&mut self, name: &str, span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        if let Some(symbol) = self.scopes.lookup(name) {\n            return symbol.ty.clone();\n        }\n        if let Some(user) = self.user_types.get(name) {\n            return match user {\n                UserType::Data { .. } => Ty::Data(name.to_owned()),\n                UserType::Enum { .. } => Ty::Enum(name.to_owned()),\n            };\n        }\n        self.error(\"E0201\", format!(\"undefined name `{name}`\"), span);\n        Ty::Unknown\n    }\n\n    /// The type of `receiver.name`.\n    fn field_type(&mut self, receiver: &Ty, name: &str, span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        match receiver {\n            Ty::Data(type_name) => {\n                let Some(UserType::Data { fields }) = self.user_types.get(type_name) else {\n                    return Ty::Unknown;\n                };\n                match fields.iter().find(|(field, _)| field == name) {\n                    Some((_, ty)) => ty.clone(),\n                    None => {\n                        self.error(\n                            \"E0304\",\n                            format!(\"`{type_name}` has no field `{name}`\"),\n                            span,\n                        );\n                        Ty::Unknown\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n            other => {\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0304\",\n                    format!(\"`{other}` has no field `{name}`\"),\n                    span,\n                );\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of a call.\n    fn check_call(&mut self, callee: &Expr, args: &[Arg], span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        // A call whose callee is a type name constructs a value (§5.3).\n        if let ExprKind::Ident(name) = &callee.kind\n            && let Some(user) = self.user_types.get(name).cloned()\n        {\n            return self.check_construction(name, user, args, span);\n        }\n\n        let callee_ty = self.check_expr(callee);\n        let Ty::Fn { params, ret } = callee_ty else {\n            if callee_ty.is_unknown() {\n                // The callee already failed; still check the arguments.\n                for arg in args {\n                    self.check_expr(&arg.value);\n                }\n                return Ty::Unknown;\n            }\n            self.error(\n                \"E0303\",\n                format!(\"`{callee_ty}` is not callable\"),\n                callee.span,\n            );\n            return Ty::Unknown;\n        };\n\n        // Positional and named arguments are matched by position; named\n        // arguments reorder against the declared parameter names where known.\n        if args.len() != params.len() {\n            self.error(\n                \"E0302\",\n                format!(\n                    \"this function takes {} argument(s) but {} were given\",\n                    params.len(),\n                    args.len()\n                ),\n                span,\n            );\n        }\n        for (index, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {\n            let found = self.check_expr(&arg.value);\n            if let Some(expected) = params.get(index)\n                && !self.assignable(expected, &found)\n            {\n                self.type_mismatch(expected, &found, arg.value.span);\n            }\n        }\n        (*ret).clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Checks `Type(field: value, ...)` or `Variant(payload, ...)`.\n    fn check_construction(\n        &mut self,\n        name: &str,\n        user: UserType,\n        args: &[Arg],\n        span: orv_syntax::Span,\n    ) -> Ty {\n        match user {\n            UserType::Data { fields } => {\n                // Positional arguments fill fields in order; named ones must\n                // match a field name.\n                if args.len() > fields.len() {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0302\",\n                        format!(\n                            \"`{name}` has {} field(s) but {} argument(s) were given\",\n                            fields.len(),\n                            args.len()\n                        ),\n                        span,\n                    );\n                }\n                for (index, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {\n                    let expected = match &arg.name {\n                        Some(field_name) => fields\n                            .iter()\n                            .find(|(field, _)| field == field_name)\n                            .map(|(_, ty)| ty.clone()),\n                        None => fields.get(index).map(|(_, ty)| ty.clone()),\n                    };\n                    let found = self.check_expr(&arg.value);\n                    match expected {\n                        Some(expected) => {\n                            if !self.assignable(&expected, &found) {\n                                self.type_mismatch(&expected, &found, arg.value.span);\n                            }\n                        }\n                        None => {\n                            let label = arg.name.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| index.to_string());\n                            self.error(\n                                \"E0304\",\n                                format!(\"`{name}` has no field `{label}`\"),\n                                arg.value.span,\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Ty::Data(name.to_owned())\n            }\n            UserType::Enum { variants } => {\n                // A call on the enum name itself is only valid for a single\n                // unit variant; payload construction goes through the variant\n                // expression form handled by `ident_type` below.\n                let _ = variants;\n                self.error(\n                    \"E0303\",\n                    format!(\"`{name}` is an enum; construct a variant instead\"),\n                    span,\n                );\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of `receiver[index]`.\n    fn index_type(&mut self, receiver: &Ty, index: &Ty, span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        match receiver {\n            Ty::List(element) => {\n                if !matches!(index, Ty::Int | Ty::Unknown) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Int, index, span);\n                }\n                (**element).clone()\n            }\n            Ty::Map(key, value) => {\n                if !self.assignable(key, index) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(key, index, span);\n                }\n                (**value).clone()\n            }\n            Ty::Str => {\n                if !matches!(index, Ty::Int | Ty::Unknown) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Int, index, span);\n                }\n                Ty::Str\n            }\n            Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n            other => {\n                self.error(\"E0303\", format!(\"`{other}` cannot be indexed\"), span);\n                Ty::Unknown\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of a prefix operation.\n    fn unary_type(&mut self, op: UnaryOp, operand: &Ty, span: orv_syntax::Span) -> Ty {\n        match op {\n            UnaryOp::Neg => {\n                if !operand.is_numeric() && !operand.is_unknown() {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0301\",\n                        format!(\"cannot negate `{operand}`\"),\n                        span,\n                    );\n                    return Ty::Unknown;\n                }\n                operand.clone()\n            }\n            UnaryOp::Not => {\n                if !operand.is_bool() && !operand.is_unknown() {\n                    self.error(\n                        \"E0301\",\n                        format!(\"`not` expects `Bool`, found `{operand}`\"),\n                        span,\n                    );\n                    return Ty::Unknown;\n                }\n                Ty::Bool\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The type of a binary operation.\n    fn binary_type(\n        &mut self,\n        op: BinaryOp,\n        left: &Ty,\n        right: &Ty,\n        span: orv_syntax::Span,\n    ) -> Ty {\n        use BinaryOp::*;\n        match op {\n            Coalesce => {\n                // `x ?? default` unwraps an optional, or passes a concrete\n                // value through (§5.3).\n                match left {\n                    Ty::Optional(inner) => {\n                        if !self.assignable(inner, right) {\n                            self.type_mismatch(inner, right, span);\n                        }\n                        (**inner).clone()\n                    }\n                    Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n                    concrete => {\n                        if !self.assignable(concrete, right) {\n                            self.type_mismatch(concrete, right, span);\n                        }\n                        concrete.clone()\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Or | And => {\n                if !left.is_bool() && !left.is_unknown() {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Bool, left, span);\n                }\n                if !right.is_bool() && !right.is_unknown() {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Bool, right, span);\n                }\n                Ty::Bool\n            }\n            Eq | NotEq => {\n                if !self.assignable(left, right) && !self.assignable(right, left) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(left, right, span);\n                }\n                Ty::Bool\n            }\n            Lt | Le | Gt | Ge => {\n                if !self.comparable(left, right) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(left, right, span);\n                }\n                Ty::Bool\n            }\n            Range | RangeInclusive => {\n                if !matches!(left, Ty::Int | Ty::Unknown) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Int, left, span);\n                }\n                if !matches!(right, Ty::Int | Ty::Unknown) {\n                    self.type_mismatch(&Ty::Int, right, span);\n                }\n                Ty::List(Box::new(Ty::Int))\n            }\n            Add => {\n                // ## Assistant (Code · Deepseek 4.1 Flash · 7.1s)

The spec is silent on the bare-IDENT ambiguity. This is a genuine design decision requiring a short ADR (per the task's own rule). I'll adopt the simplest rule consistent with the grammar and with how `data`/`enum` are named:

**A bare `IDENT` in a pattern is a variant pattern when the scrutinee is an `enum` and the name is an uppercase-initial name matching a declared variant OR is not a declared local; otherwise it binds.** That's getting complicated.

Simpler and defensible: **when the scrutinee is an enum, a bare `IDENT` is resolved as a variant if one matches, otherwise it binds** (current behavior) — and an unknown uppercase name is *not* an error. Let me instead make the rule explicit and simple: since §5.2 gives `_` for wildcards and names for bindings, and §5.3 says matches must be exhaustive, a wrong variant name is caught by **exhaustiveness** (`E0320`), not by the pattern itself. That's cleaner: my `unknown_variant_reports_e0321` test should be replaced by an exhaustiveness check.

But exhaustiveness is M5 per §12. For the alpha, I'll document the rule as: bare name binds unless it matches a variant; unknown variants are not detectable, which is a known limitation. Let me adjust the test and record the decision.

The `orv check` subcommand (SPEC §10).\n//!\n//! Lexes, parses and type-checks a file without executing it. Diagnostics go to\n//! stderr in the stable compact form (§8.1) when stderr is not a terminal, and\n//! the exit code is `1` when anything failed (SPEC §10).\n\nuse std::io::{IsTerminal, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse orv_sema::check as sema_check;\nuse orv_syntax::{Parser, SourceMap, lex};\n\nuse crate::cli::SubcommandOutcome;\nuse crate::diag;\n\n/// Runs the front end over `path`.\npub fn run(path: &Path) -> SubcommandOutcome {\n    let mut sources = SourceMap::new();\n    let id = match sources.load(path) {\n        Ok(id) => id,\n        Err(err) => {\n            let _ = writeln!(\n                std::io::stderr(),\n                \"error: cannot read {}: {err}\",\n                path.display()\n            );\n            return SubcommandOutcome::Usage;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let Some(file) = sources.file(id) else {\n        let _ = writeln!(\n            std::io::stderr(),\n            \"error: internal source map failure for {}\",\n            path.display()\n        );\n        return SubcommandOutcome::Usage;\n    };\n\n    // Stage 1: lex (diagnostics are lexical-first, ADR 0008 amend rule 2).\n    let (tokens, lexical) = lex(file);\n    // Stage 2: parse, suppressing parser diagnostics that intersect a lexical\n    // one (rule 3), and never re-lexing a best-effort `Expr.src` (rule 4).\n    let mut parser = Parser::new(&tokens, lexical);\n    let parsed = parser.parse_program();\n\n    let mut diagnostics: Vec<orv_syntax::Diagnostic> = parsed.diagnostics.into_vec();\n\n    // Stage 3: type check, but only when stages 1 and 2 were clean — a broken\n    // parse has no meaningful types to check (rule 5). The AST is still passed\n    // through when there were no errors in the previous stages.\n    if parsed.program.is_some() && !has_error(&diagnostics) {\n        let Some(program) = parsed.program else {\n            return SubcommandOutcome::Failure;\n        };\n        let checked = sema_check(&program);\n        diagnostics.extend(checked.diagnostics);\n    }\n\n    let failed = has_error(&diagnostics);\n    report(&sources, &diagnostics);\n\n    if failed {\n        SubcommandOutcome::Failure\n    } else {\n        SubcommandOutcome::Ok\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whether any diagnostic is an error.\nfn has_error(diagnostics: &[orv_syntax::Diagnostic]) -> bool {\n    diagnostics\n        .iter()\n        .any(|d| d.severity == orv_syntax::Severity::Error)\n}\n\n/// Writes every diagnostic to stderr.\nfn report(sources: &SourceMap, diagnostics: &[orv_syntax::Diagnostic]) {\n    let pretty = std::io::stderr().is_terminal();\n    for diagnostic in diagnostics {\n        let _ = if pretty {\n            diag::render_or_compact(sources, diagnostic)\n        } else {\n            diag::print_compact(sources, diagnostic)\n        };\n    }\n}\nEOF\npython3 - <<'PY'\np='crates/orv-cli/src/main.rs'\nt=open(p).read()\nt=t.replace(\"mod ast;\\nmod cli;\",\"mod ast;\\nmod check;\\nmod cli;\")\nopen(p,'w').write(t)\np='crates/orv-cli/src/cli.rs'\nt=open(p).read()\nt=t.replace('''    /// Print the Orvane version.\n    Version,''','''    /// Print the Orvane version.\n    Version,\n    /// Type-check a file without running it.\n    Check {\n        /// The `.orv` file to check.\n        file: PathBuf,\n    },''')\nt=t.replace('''        Command::Ast { file } => crate::ast::run(&file),\n    };''','''        Command::Ast { file } => crate::ast::run(&file),\n        Command::Check { file } => crate::check::run(&file),\n    };''')\nopen(p,'w').write(t)\nPY\ncargo build -q -p orv-cli 2>&1 | head -20 && ./target/debug/orv check /tmp/fizz.orv; echo \"fizz exit=$?\"; ./target/debug/orv check /tmp/a.orv; echo \"ok exit=$?\"",

An uncaught failure reaches `main` as a diagnostic and exit code 1.\n\nuse std::rc::Rc;\n\nuse orv_syntax::Span;\n\n/// A runtime failure.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Failure {\n    /// A stable machine-readable kind, e.g. `DivisionByZero`.\n    pub kind: FailureKind,\n    /// A human-readable message.\n    pub message: Rc<str>,\n    /// The call stack at the point of failure, innermost last.\n    pub trace: Rc<Vec<Frame>>,\n    /// Where it happened.\n    pub span: Span,\n}\n\n/// The kinds of runtime failure in the alpha (SPEC §5.5, §5.3).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum FailureKind {\n    /// `1 / 0` or `1 % 0` (`R0001`).\n    DivisionByZero,\n    /// Integer overflow (`R0002`).\n    Overflow,\n    /// An index past the end of a list or string (`R0003`).\n    IndexOutOfBounds,\n    /// `assert` failed (`AssertionFailed`).\n    AssertionFailed,\n    /// A map lookup for a missing key.\n    MissingKey,\n    /// A runtime operation that is not supported in the alpha.\n    Unsupported,\n}\n\nimpl FailureKind {\n    /// The stable name used in messages and (later) JSON output.\n    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FailureKind::DivisionByZero => \"DivisionByZero\",\n            FailureKind::Overflow => \"Overflow\",\n            FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds => \"IndexOutOfBounds\",\n            FailureKind::AssertionFailed => \"AssertionFailed\",\n            FailureKind::MissingKey => \"MissingKey\",\n            FailureKind::Unsupported => \"Unsupported\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The `Rxxxx` diagnostic code from `docs/errors.md`.\n    pub const fn code(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FailureKind::DivisionByZero => \"R0001\",\n            FailureKind::Overflow => \"R0002\",\n            FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds => \"R0003\",\n            FailureKind::AssertionFailed => \"R0001\",\n            FailureKind::MissingKey => \"R0003\",\n            FailureKind::Unsupported => \"R0010\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// One frame of the Orvane call stack.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Frame {\n    /// The function name, or `<main>`.\n    pub function: Rc<str>,\n    /// Where the call happened.\n    pub span: Span,\n}\n\nimpl Failure {\n    /// Creates a failure with no stack.\n    pub fn new(kind: FailureKind, message: impl Into<Rc<str>>, span: Span) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            kind,\n            message: message.into(),\n            trace: Rc::new(Vec::new()),\n            span,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Attaches a call stack.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn with_trace(mut self, trace: Vec<Frame>) -> Self {\n        self.trace = Rc::new(trace);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Structural equality, used by `Result` values (§5.3).\n    pub fn equals(&self, other: &Failure) -> bool {\n        self.kind == other.kind && self.message == other.message\n    }\n}\n\n/// The structured rendering used inside `Err(...)` and in diagnostics.\n///\n/// Matches §5.5's shape: `Failure(kind: \"...\", message: \"...\")`.\npub fn render(failure: &Failure) -> String {\n    format!(\n        \"Failure(kind: {:?}, message: {:?})\",\n        failure.kind.as_str(),\n        failure.message.as_ref()\n    )\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use orv_syntax::{FileId, Span};\n\n    fn span() -> Span {\n        Span::point(FileId(0), 0)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn renders_the_spec_shape() {\n        let failure = Failure::new(FailureKind::DivisionByZero, \"division by zero\", span());\n        assert_eq!(\n            render(&failure),\n            \"Failure(kind: \\\"DivisionByZero\\\", message: \\\"division by zero\\\")\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kinds_have_stable_names_and_codes() {\n        assert_eq!(FailureKind::DivisionByZero.as_str(), \"DivisionByZero\");\n        assert_eq!(FailureKind::DivisionByZero.code(), \"R0001\");\n        assert_eq!(FailureKind::Overflow.code(), \"R0002\");\n        assert_eq!(FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds.code(), \"R0003\");\n span: span(),\n        }]);\n        let b = Failure::new(FailureKind::Overflow, \"boom\", span());\n        assert!(a.equals(&b));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_kinds_are_not_equal() {\n        let a = Failure::new(FailureKind::Overflow, \"boom\", span());\n        let b = Failure::new(FailureKind::MissingKey, \"boom\", span());\n        assert!(!a.equals(&b));\n    }\n}\n",

},\n}\n\n/// A function value with its name (for diagnostics) and arity.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Closure {\n    /// The name shown in `<fn name>` and in stack frames.\n    pub name: Rc<str>,\n normalize_index(position, elements.len()).ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds,\n                        format!(\"index {position} is out of bounds for a list of length {}\", elements.len()),\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                })?;\n                elements[position] = value;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Value::Map(entries) => {\n                let Some(key) = MapKey::from_value(index) else {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        \"map keys must be Int, Str or Bool\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                };\n                entries.borrow_mut().insert(key, value);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            other => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"`{}` cannot be indexed for assignment\", other.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The values a `for` loop iterates.\n    fn iterable(&mut self, value: &Value, span: Span) -> Result<Vec<Value>, Box<Failure>> {\n        match value {\n            Value::List(elements) => Ok(elements.borrow().clone()),\n            Value::Map(entries) => Ok(entries.borrow().keys().iter().map(MapKey::to_value).collect()),\n            Value::Str(text) => Ok(text\n                .chars()\n                .map(|c| Value::str(c.to_string()))\n                .collect()),\n            other => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"`{}` is not iterable\", other.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Looks a field up on a value.\n    fn field(&mut self, value: &Value, name: &str, span: Span) -> EvalResult {\n        match value {\n            Value::Data { name: type_name, fields } => fields\n                .iter()\n                .find(|(field, _)| field.as_ref() == name)\n                .map(|(_, value)| value.clone())\n                .ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        format!(\"`{type_name}` has no field `{name}`\"),\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                }),\n            other => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"`{}` has no field `{name}`\", other.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Indexes a list, map or string.\n    fn index(&mut self, container: &Value, index: &Value, span: Span) -> EvalResult {\n        match container {\n            Value::List(elements) => {\n                let Some(position) = index.as_int() else {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        \"list index must be an `Int`\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                };\n                let elements = elements.borrow();\n                let position = normalize_index(position, elements.len()).ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds,\n                        format!(\n                            \"index {position} is out of bounds for a list of length {}\",\n                            elements.len()\n                        ),\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                })?;\n                Ok(elements[position].clone())\n            }\n            Value::Map(entries) => {\n                let Some(key) = MapKey::from_value(index) else {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        \"map keys must be Int, Str or Bool\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                };\n                entries.borrow().get(&key).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::MissingKey,\n                        format!(\"key `{key}` not found\"),\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                })\n            }\n            Value::Str(text) => {\n                let Some(position) = index.as_int() else {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        \"string index must be an `Int`\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                };\n                let characters: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();\n                let position = normalize_index(position, characters.len()).ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::IndexOutOfBounds,\n                        format!(\n                            \"index {position} is out of bounds for a string of length {}\",\n                            characters.len()\n                        ),\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                })?;\n                Ok(Value::str(characters[position].to_string()))\n            }\n            other => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"`{}` cannot be indexed\", other.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Calls --------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Evaluates a call.\n    fn eval_call(&mut self, callee: &Expr, args: &[orv_syntax::Arg], span: Span) -> EvalResult {\n        // A `data` constructor: the callee names a type, handled by the caller\n        // building the value from the declaration in scope.\n        if let ExprKind::Ident(name) = &callee.kind\n            && let Some(value) = self.try_construct(name, args, span)?\n        {\n            return Ok(value);\n        }\n        // A variant constructor.\n        if let ExprKind::Ident(name) = &callee.kind\n            && let Some(value) = self.try_variant(name, args, span)?\n        {\n            return Ok(value);\n        }\n\n        let callee_value = self.eval(callee)?;\n        let Value::Function(function) = callee_value else {\n            return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"`{}` is not callable\", callee_value.ty()),\n                span,\n            )));\n        };\n\n        let mut evaluated = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());\n        for arg in args {\n            evaluated.push(self.eval(&arg.value)?);\n        }\n        self.call_function(&function, evaluated, span)\n    }\n\n    /// Calls a function value with already-evaluated arguments.\n    pub fn call_function(\n        &mut self,\n        function: &Rc<Closure>,\n        args: Vec<Value>,\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> EvalResult {\n        if args.len() != function.arity {\n            return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\n                    \"`{}` takes {} argument(s) but {} were given\",\n                    function.name,\n                    function.arity,\n                    args.len()\n                ),\n                span,\n            )));\n        }\n        // A builtin is represented by a function whose closure has no AST body.\n        if let Some(builtin) = builtins::lookup(&function.name) {\n            return builtin(self, &args, span);\n        }\n\n        if self.depth >= MAX_CALL_DEPTH {\n            return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Overflow,\n                format!(\"call depth exceeded {MAX_CALL_DEPTH} (possible infinite recursion)\"),\n                span,\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let names = function.param_names();\n        let previous_env = std::mem::replace(&mut self.env, self.call_env(function));\n        self.env.push();\n        for (name, value) in names.iter().zip(args.into_iter()) {\n            self.env.define(Rc::from(name.as_str()), value, false);\n        }\n        self.frames.push(Frame {\n            function: function.name.clone(),\n            span,\n        });\n        self.depth += 1;\n\n        let outcome = match function.block() {\n            Some(block) => self.eval_statements(&block.statements),\n            None => match function.lambda_body() {\n                Some(body) => {\n                    let body = body.clone();\n                    self.eval(&body)\n                }\n                None => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    format!(\"`{}` has no body\", function.name),\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            },\n        };\n\n        self.depth = self.depth.saturating_sub(1);\n        self.frames.pop();\n        self.env.pop();\n        self.env = previous_env;\n\n        match outcome {\n            Ok(value) => Ok(value),\n            // A `return` inside the body is the function's value.\n            Err(failure) => match unpack_return(&failure) {\n                Some(value) => Ok(value),\n                None => Err(failure),\n            },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The environment a call starts from.\n    ///\n    /// A named function is top-level, so it sees the global scope. A lambda\n    /// sees the scope it captured when the lambda value was created.\n    fn call_env(&self, function: &Rc<Closure>) -> Env {\n        match &function.callable {\n            crate::function::Callable::Named(_) => self.global.clone(),\n            crate::function::Callable::Lambda { captured, .. } => captured.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Builds a `data` value when `name` is a declared type.\n    fn try_construct(\n        &mut self,\n        name: &str,\n        args: &[orv_syntax::Arg],\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, Box<Failure>> {\n        let Some(schema) = builtins::data_schema(self, name) else {\n            return Ok(None);\n        };\n        let mut fields: Vec<(Rc<str>, Value)> = Vec::with_capacity(schema.len());\n        for (index, (field_name, _ty)) in schema.iter().enumerate() {\n            fields.push((Rc::from(field_name.as_str()), Value::None));\n        }\n        for (index, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {\n            let value = self.eval(&arg.value)?;\n            let position = match &arg.name {\n                Some(field) => schema.iter().position(|(name, _)| name == field),\n                None => Some(index),\n            };\n            match position {\n                Some(position) if position < fields.len() => {\n                    fields[position] = (fields[position].0.clone(), value);\n                }\n                _ => {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        format!(\"`{name}` has no field for this argument\"),\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(Some(Value::Data {\n            name: Rc::from(name),\n            fields: Rc::new(fields),\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Builds an `enum` variant when `name` is one.\n    fn try_variant(\n        &mut self,\n        name: &str,\n        args: &[orv_syntax::Arg],\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, Box<Failure>> {\n        let Some((enum_name, arity)) = builtins::variant_schema(self, name) else {\n            return Ok(None);\n        };\n        let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());\n        for arg in args {\n            payload.push(self.eval(&arg.value)?);\n        }\n        if payload.len() != arity {\n            return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\n                    \"variant `{name}` takes {arity} field(s) but {} were given\",\n                    payload.len()\n                ),\n                span,\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(Some(Value::Variant {\n            enum_name: Rc::from(enum_name.as_str()),\n            variant: Rc::from(name),\n            payload: Rc::new(payload),\n        }))\n    }\n\n    // --- Operators ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Applies a unary operator.\n    fn unary(&mut self, op: orv_syntax::UnaryOp, value: Value, span: Span) -> EvalResult {\n        match op {\n            orv_syntax::UnaryOp::Not => match value.as_bool() {\n                Some(value) => Ok(Value::Bool(!value)),\n                None => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    format!(\"`not` expects `Bool`, found `{}`\", value.ty()),\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            },\n            orv_syntax::UnaryOp::Neg => match value {\n                Value::Int(value) => value.checked_neg().map(Value::Int).ok_or_else(|| {\n                    Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Overflow,\n                        \"integer overflow negating the minimum `Int`\",\n                        span,\n                    ))\n                }),\n                Value::Float(value) => Ok(Value::Float(-value)),\n                other => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    format!(\"cannot negate `{}`\", other.ty()),\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates a binary operation, short-circuiting `and`/`or`.\n    fn eval_binary(\n        &mut self,\n        op: orv_syntax::BinaryOp,\n        left: &Expr,\n        right: &Expr,\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> EvalResult {\n        use orv_syntax::BinaryOp;\n        match op {\n            BinaryOp::And => {\n                let left = self.eval(left)?;\n                match left.as_bool() {\n                    Some(false) => return Ok(Value::Bool(false)),\n                    Some(true) => {}\n                    None => {\n                        return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                            FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                            format!(\"`and` expects `Bool`, found `{}`\", left.ty()),\n                            span,\n                        )));\n                    }\n                }\n                let right = self.eval(right)?;\n                match right.as_bool() {\n                    Some(value) => Ok(Value::Bool(value)),\n                    None => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        format!(\"`and` expects `Bool`, found `{}`\", right.ty()),\n                        span,\n                    ))),\n                }\n            }\n            BinaryOp::Or => {\n                let left = self.eval(left)?;\n                match left.as_bool() {\n                    Some(true) => return Ok(Value::Bool(true)),\n                    Some(false) => {}\n                    None => {\n                        return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                            FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                            format!(\"`or` expects `Bool`, found `{}`\", left.ty()),\n                            span,\n                        )));\n                    }\n                }\n                let right = self.eval(right)?;\n                match right.as_bool() {\n                    Some(value) => Ok(Value::Bool(value)),\n                    None => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        format!(\"`or` expects `Bool`, found `{}`\", right.ty()),\n                        span,\n                    ))),\n                }\n            }\n            BinaryOp::Coalesce => {\n                let left = self.eval(left)?;\n                match left {\n                    Value::None => self.eval(right),\n                    other => Ok(other),\n                }\n            }\n            _ => {\n                let left = self.eval(left)?;\n                let right = self.eval(right)?;\n                self.binary_op(op, left, right, span)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Applies a binary operator to two values.\n    fn binary_op(\n        &mut self,\n        op: orv_syntax::BinaryOp,\n        left: Value,\n        right: Value,\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> EvalResult {\n        use orv_syntax::BinaryOp;\n        match op {\n            BinaryOp::Eq => Ok(Value::Bool(left.equals(&right))),\n            BinaryOp::NotEq => Ok(Value::Bool(!left.equals(&right))),\n            BinaryOp::Lt | BinaryOp::Le | BinaryOp::Gt | BinaryOp::Ge => {\n                let ordering = self.compare(&left, &right, span)?;\n                let result = match op {\n                    BinaryOp::Lt => ordering.is_lt(),\n                    BinaryOp::Le => ordering.is_le(),\n                    BinaryOp::Gt => ordering.is_gt(),\n                    _ => ordering.is_ge(),\n                };\n                Ok(Value::Bool(result))\n            }\n            BinaryOp::Range | BinaryOp::RangeInclusive => {\n                let (Some(start), Some(end)) = (left.as_int(), right.as_int()) else {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        \"range bounds must be `Int`\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                };\n                let inclusive = matches!(op, BinaryOp::RangeInclusive);\n                Ok(Value::list(int_range(start, end, inclusive)))\n            }\n            BinaryOp::Add => match (&left, &right) {\n                // String concatenation (§5.3).\n                (Value::Str(a), Value::Str(b)) => {\n                    let mut text = String::with_capacity(a.len() + b.len());\n                    text.push_str(a);\n                    text.push_str(b);\n                    Ok(Value::str(text))\n                }\n                (Value::List(a), Value::List(b)) => {\n                    let mut combined = a.borrow().clone();\n                    combined.extend(b.borrow().iter().cloned());\n                    Ok(Value::list(combined))\n                }\n                _ => self.arithmetic(op, left, right, span),\n            },\n            BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::Mul | BinaryOp::Div | BinaryOp::Rem => {\n                self.arithmetic(op, left, right, span)\n            }\n            // Handled by `eval_binary` before reaching here.\n            BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or | BinaryOp::Coalesce => Ok(Value::Bool(false)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Arithmetic with checked operations (§5.3: no wrap, no panic).\n    fn arithmetic(\n        &mut self,\n        op: orv_syntax::BinaryOp,\n        left: Value,\n        right: Value,\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> EvalResult {\n        use orv_syntax::BinaryOp;\n\n        // Float if either side is one; otherwise integer arithmetic.\n        if matches!(left, Value::Float(_)) || matches!(right, Value::Float(_)) {\n            let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (as_float(&left), as_float(&right)) else {\n                return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    format!(\"cannot apply `{}` to these values\", op.as_str()),\n                    span,\n                )));\n            };\n            if matches!(op, BinaryOp::Div) && b == 0.0 {\n                return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::DivisionByZero,\n                    \"division by zero\",\n                    span,\n                )));\n            }\n            let result = match op {\n                BinaryOp::Add => a + b,\n                BinaryOp::Sub => a - b,\n                BinaryOp::Mul => a * b,\n                BinaryOp::Div => a / b,\n                BinaryOp::Rem => a % b,\n                _ => {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                        format!(\"unsupported float operator `{}`\", op.as_str()),\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                }\n            };\n            return Ok(Value::Float(result));\n        }\n\n        let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (left.as_int(), right.as_int()) else {\n            return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\n                    \"cannot apply `{}` to `{}` and `{}`\",\n                    op.as_str(),\n                    left.ty(),\n                    right.ty()\n                ),\n                span,\n            )));\n        };\n\n        let result = match op {\n            BinaryOp::Add => a.checked_add(b),\n            BinaryOp::Sub => a.checked_sub(b),\n            BinaryOp::Mul => a.checked_mul(b),\n            BinaryOp::Div => {\n                if b == 0 {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::DivisionByZero,\n                        \"division by zero\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                }\n                a.checked_div(b)\n            }\n            BinaryOp::Rem => {\n                if b == 0 {\n                    return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                        FailureKind::DivisionByZero,\n                        \"division by zero\",\n                        span,\n                    )));\n                }\n                a.checked_rem(b)\n            }\n            _ => None,\n        };\n        result.map(Value::Int).ok_or_else(|| {\n            Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Overflow,\n                format!(\"integer overflow in `{}`\", op.as_str()),\n                span,\n            ))\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Orders two comparable values.\n    fn compare(\n        &mut self,\n        left: &Value,\n        right: &Value,\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> Result<std::cmp::Ordering, Box<Failure>> {\n        match (left, right) {\n            (Value::Int(a), Value::Int(b)) => Ok(a.cmp(b)),\n            (Value::Float(a), Value::Float(b)) => a\n                .partial_cmp(b)\n                .ok_or_else(|| Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    \"cannot order `NaN`\",\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            (Value::Int(a), Value::Float(b)) => (*a as f64)\n                .partial_cmp(b)\n                .ok_or_else(|| Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    \"cannot order `NaN`\",\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            (Value::Float(a), Value::Int(b)) => a\n                .partial_cmp(&(*b as f64))\n                .ok_or_else(|| Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    \"cannot order `NaN`\",\n                    span,\n                ))),\n            (Value::Str(a), Value::Str(b)) => Ok(a.cmp(b)),\n            _ => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"cannot compare `{}` and `{}`\", left.ty(), right.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Applies `expr as Type` (SPEC §5.3).\n    fn cast(&mut self, value: Value, ty: &orv_syntax::Type, span: Span) -> EvalResult {\n        let target = match orv_sema::ty::resolve_type(ty) {\n            Ok(target) => target,\n            Err(_) => {\n                return Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                    FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                    \"invalid cast target\",\n                    span,\n                )));\n            }\n        };\n        match (&value, &target) {\n            (Value::Int(value), Ty::Float) => Ok(Value::Float(*value as f64)),\n            (value, target) if &value.ty() == target => Ok(value.clone()),\n            _ => Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n                FailureKind::Unsupported,\n                format!(\"cannot cast `{}` to `{target}`\", value.ty()),\n                span,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Match --------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Evaluates a `match`, first arm that matches wins (§5.2).\n    fn eval_match(\n        &mut self,\n        value: &Value,\n        arms: &[orv_syntax::MatchArm],\n        span: Span,\n    ) -> EvalResult {\n        for arm in arms {\n            self.env.push();\n            let matched = self.match_pattern(&arm.pattern, value);\n            if matched {\n                let guard_ok = match &arm.guard {\n                    Some(guard) => {\n                        let guard_value = self.eval(guard)?;\n                        guard_value.as_bool().unwrap_or(false)\n                    }\n                    None => true,\n                };\n                if guard_ok {\n                    let outcome = self.eval(&arm.body);\n                    self.env.pop();\n                    return outcome;\n                }\n            }\n            self.env.pop();\n        }\n        // The checker ensures exhaustiveness in a later milestone; the\n        // interpreter still must not panic, so an unmatched value is a failure.\n        Err(Box::new(Failure::new(\n            FailureKind::Unsupported,\n            format!(\"no `match` arm matched `{}`\", display(value)),\n            span,\n        )))\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `pattern` matches `value`, binding names in the current scope.\n    fn match_pattern(&mut self, pattern: &orv_syntax::Pattern, value: &Value) -> bool {\n        use orv_syntax::PatternKind;\n        match &pattern.kind {\n            PatternKind::Wildcard => true,\n            PatternKind::Bind(name) => {\n                // A bare name that is a declared variant is a variant pattern\n                // (ADR 0015); otherwise it binds.\n                if let Some((_, arity)) = builtins::variant_schema(self, name) {\n                    return match value {\n                        Value::Variant {\n                            variant, payload, ..\n                        } => variant.as_ref() == name && payload.len() == arity,\n                        _ => false,\n                    };\n                }\n                self.env\n                    .define(Rc::from(name.as_str()), value.clone(), false);\n                true\n            }\n            PatternKind::Literal(literal) => literal_value(literal).equals(value),\n            PatternKind::Variant { name, fields } => match value {\n                Value::Variant {\n                    variant, payload, ..\n                } if variant.as_ref() == name => {\n                    if payload.len() != fields.len() {\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                    fields\n                        .iter()\n                        .zip(payload.iter())\n                        .all(|(pattern, value)| self.match_pattern(pattern, value))\n                }\n                _ => false,\n            },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The value of a literal.\nfn literal_value(literal: &Literal) -> Value {\n    match literal {\n        Literal::Int(value) => Value::Int(*value),\n        Literal::Float(value) => Value::Float(*value),\n        Literal::Bool(value) => Value::Bool(*value),\n        // Interpolation is not evaluated in the alpha (ADR 0012): the literal\n        // text parts are concatenated, `{...}` parts are kept verbatim.\n        Literal::Str(parts) => {\n            let mut text = String::new();\n            for part in parts {\n                match part {\n                    orv_syntax::StrPart::Lit(lit) => text.push_str(lit),\n                    orv_syntax::StrPart::Expr { src, .. } => {\n                        text.push('{');\n                        text.push_str(src);\n                        text.push('}');\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Value::str(text)\n        }\n        Literal::None => Value::None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// A float view of a numeric value.\nfn as_float(value: &Value) -> Option<f64> {\n    match value {\n        Value::Int(value) => Some(*value as f64),\n        Value::Float(value) => Some(*value),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Normalizes a possibly negative index against a length.\n///\n/// Negative indices count from the end, matching the usual convention.\nfn normalize_index(index: i64, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {\n    let len = len as i64;\n    let resolved = if index < 0 { len + index } else { index };\n    if resolved < 0 || resolved >= len {\n        None\n    } else {\n        usize::try_from(resolved).ok()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The integers in a range.\nfn int_range(start: i64, end: i64, inclusive: bool) -> Vec<Value> {\n    let mut values = Vec::new();\n    let mut current = start;\n    let condition = |value: i64| if inclusive { value <= end } else { value < end };\n    // A range is bounded by the input; an absurd span is capped so a The runtime reports nothing here:\n    // a 10-million-element range is legal but pointless, so the cap is generous.\n    const MAX_RANGE: usize = 10_000_000;\n    while condition(current) && values.len() < MAX_RANGE {\n        values.push(Value::Int(current));\n        match current.checked_add(1) {\n            Some(next) => current = next,\n            None => break,\n        }\n    }\n    values\n}\n\n/// A `return` in flight, carried as a failure-like control result.\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct ReturnSignal {\n    value: Value,\n}\n\nimpl ReturnSignal {\n    fn new(value: Value) -> Self {\n        Self { value }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Renders a `ReturnSignal` as a [`Failure`] so it can travel in `Err`.\nimpl ReturnSignal {\n    fn into_failure(self, span: Span) -> Failure {\n        Failure {\n            kind: FailureKind::Unsupported,\n            message: Rc::from(RETURN_MARKER),\n            trace: Rc::new(Vec::new()),\n            span,\n        }\n        .tap_value(self.value)\n    }\n}\n\nconst RETURN_MARKER: &str = \"\\u{0}return\";\n\n/// Carries a value alongside a control-flow marker.\n///\n/// The interpreter uses `Err(Box<Failure>)` as its control channel, so `return`,\n/// `break` and `continue` travel as failures with a private marker message. failure: Option<Box<Failure>>,\n}\n\nimpl RunOutcome {\n    /// Whether the program completed without an escaping failure.\n    pub fn is_ok(&self) -> bool {\n        self.failure.is_none()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Registers a program's declarations in a fresh interpreter.\npub fn prepare(program: &Program) -> Interpreter {\n    let mut interpreter = Interpreter::new();\n    register(&mut interpreter, program);\n    interpreter\n}\n\n/// Registers an already-created interpreter's program declarations.\npub fn register(interpreter: &mut Interpreter, program: &Program) {\n    // Functions first, so a later function can call an earlier one regardless\n    // of declaration order (the checker already allows either order).\n    for item in &program.items {\n        if let ItemKind::Fn(decl) = &item.kind {\n            let closure = Rc::new(crate::function::Closure::named(Rc::new(decl.clone())));\n            interpreter.define_function(&decl.name, closure);\n        }\n    }\n    for item in &program.items {\n        register_types(interpreter, item);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Registers the type schemas carried by one item.\nfn register_types(interpreter: &mut Interpreter, item: &Item) {\n    match &item.kind {\n        ItemKind::Data(decl) => {\n            let fields = decl\n                .fields\n                .iter()\n                .map(|field| );\n            }\n        }\n        ItemKind::Fn(_) | ItemKind::Use(_) => {}\n    }\n}\n\n/// Runs `program`'s `main`.\n///\n/// A program without `main` is not an error here: `orv check` covers
